prompt: Build the Mount Rushmore of interstate highways. Numbers only, then defend one of them with your whole chest.
response:
10, 40, 80, 95

### Defense of Interstate 40

I-40 is the undisputed soul of the American interstate system because it is the only route that perfectly synthesizes engineering necessity, cultural mythology, and geographic narrative into a single 2,555-mile ribbon of asphalt. While I-10 hugs the southern border and I-80 traces the northern tier, I-40 cuts through the *heart* of the continent’s most defining landscape, serving as the direct successor to Route 66 and carrying its ghost in every mile. It doesn’t just connect cities; it connects eras, threading the needle between the Appalachian spine and the Mojave Desert while showcasing the full geological biography of North America.

No other interstate offers this level of cinematic and historical weight. Driving westbound on I-40 is a masterclass in American geography: you ascend through the Blue Ridge, navigate the complex engineering of the Tennessee River valley, cross the Mississippi Delta, traverse the Llano Estacado, climb the Sangre de Cristo Mountains, descend into the Painted Desert, and finally breach the Sierra Nevada at Barstow. It is the only east-west interstate that feels like a journey through time as much as space, preserving the romantic ideal of the open road while functioning as a critical commercial artery for the Sun Belt’s economic rise. I-80 is utilitarian, I-10 is coastal, and I-95 is a congested corridor, but I-40 remains the definitive American road trip etched in concrete.
